There is NOT ONE #include in main.c: every name is declared by the TU itself (C23 7.1.4p2), so none reaches the corpus through the include closure -- they arrive through the platform realization oracle (ffi::realizeShippedExternSymbols), which resolves by the corpus index's relPath sort, a DIFFERENT order from the include closure. That divergence is the row: MEASURED on pe64 with objdump -p over a DSS_CONFIG_ROOT copy whose memory.json named msvcrt.dll where string.json named ucrtbase.dll, the two #include orders REFUSED with F_ShippedCorpusInvariantBroken while this spelling built rc=0 with ZERO diagnostics and imported memcpy from MSVCRT.DLL -- one program, two spellings, two C runtimes, no diagnostic. The six names are the math+tgmath overlap, which is the LARGEST co-live duplicate set in the shipped corpus (34 names on elf/macho, 32 on pe: <tgmath.h> mirrors <math.h> exactly as <memory.h> mirrors <string.h>), so every call is a name for which TWO descriptors are read, compared and required to agree before anything binds. WHAT IT PINS THAT A UNIT TEST CANNOT: that the rule now runs on the hand-declared path WITHOUT refusing the shipped configuration, and that the surviving import still WORKS at runtime on every leg. A check that degenerated into 'duplicates are forbidden' fails this at BUILD time on all four targets; a check wired to the wrong side of the availability gate fails it on exactly one format.
